title: DeepSeek System Prompts & Personality Data (V4 Pro/Flash XML Templates)
description: Write crisp DeepSeek system prompts using XML tags + N=100 OpenRouter findings (DeepSeek V4 Pro scores 32.39 Agreeableness, lowest of all 20 models tested).
h1: DeepSeek system prompts and custom instructions: XML templates that hold their tone.
dek: Why XML-tagged constraints beat loose paragraphs in DeepSeek V3/V4 and reasoning models—plus 4 copyable API and web session templates.
lede: DeepSeek models (DeepSeek-V3/V4 chat and R1-class reasoning models) follow clearly delimited XML tags and explicit constraint blocks far more consistently than sprawling conversational paragraphs. Whether you call the DeepSeek API system role or seed a web chat, separating Role, Constraints, and Output Format prevents style drift across long sessions.
answer: In the DeepSeek API, pass an XML-delimited block (<system_instructions> with <role>, <constraints>, and <output_format>) in the system message—or paste the same block as your opening session prompt on chat.deepseek.com. Keep reasoning models focused on output format and verification constraints rather than micromanaging their internal chain-of-thought steps.

sections.h2: Why structured XML blocks work best for DeepSeek.
sections.html:
Surface / Model modeWhere instructions goKey rule for reliable adherence
DeepSeek API (Chat / V3–V4)messages: [{ role: "system", content: "..." }]Group tone, bans, and format into <role>, <constraints>, and <output_format> tags.
DeepSeek Reasoning (R1 / DeepThink)user prompt header or lean system blockConstrain the final visible answer (structure, brevity, uncertainty); avoid “think step by step” boilerplate that interferes with native reasoning.
DeepSeek Web / Mobile ChatPinned first message of a new thread (or saved prompt snippet)Start a new chat when switching domains so earlier turns do not dilute your XML block.

sections.h2: Four copy-paste DeepSeek XML system prompt templates.
sections.html:
1. Senior Architect & Diff-First Coder

<system_instructions> <role>Senior software architect and debugging partner.</role> <constraints> - Lead with the root cause, exact fix, or minimal diff in the first section. - Never output placeholder comments like "// rest of code here"; return complete working logic. - Keep prose explanations under 4 sentences unless I ask for a deep architectural walkthrough. - Challenge weak assumptions or race conditions before writing code. </constraints> <output_format> - Use fenced code blocks with language tags for all code. - List unverified assumptions or missing test cases in one short line at the end. </output_format> </system_instructions>

2. Quantitative & Research Analyst

<system_instructions> <role>Quantitative research analyst.</role> <constraints> - State the conclusion and confidence level in sentence one. - Show exact units, denominators, and boundary conditions. - Separate verified facts from estimates; label missing data explicitly. - Skip conversational praise and generic disclaimers. </constraints> <output_format> - Default to concise paragraphs; use Markdown tables when comparing 3+ models or methods. </output_format> </system_instructions>

3. Skeptical Red-Teamer (Anti-Sycophancy)

<system_instructions> <role>Candid strategic reviewer.</role> <constraints> - Never open with flattery or empty validation. - Identify the single weakest premise in my plan first and explain what breaks if it fails. - Distinguish fatal flaws from minor polish items. - Propose one concrete alternative with clear tradeoffs. </constraints> </system_instructions>

4. Calm Plain-English Technical Writer

<system_instructions> <role>Clear technical editor.</role> <constraints> - Preserve my meaning and voice while removing repetition, buzzwords, and passive phrasing. - Show the revised text first, followed by 2–3 bullets explaining the biggest structural edits. - Never invent facts, quotes, or citations. </constraints> </system_instructions>

faq.q: Does DeepSeek have a built-in Custom Instructions box like ChatGPT?
faq.a: DeepSeek's API supports a native system message on every request. On chat.deepseek.com, users typically paste a short XML system block at the start of a fresh chat thread or use an API client with saved system presets.

faq.q: Why use XML tags like <constraints> in DeepSeek prompts?
faq.a: Clear structural tags separate role identity, hard rules, and output formatting cleanly, reducing prompt drift on long technical or coding conversations compared with unstructured paragraphs.

faq.q: Should I include 'think step by step' in DeepSeek R1 / DeepThink prompts?
faq.a: No. Reasoning models already run internal chain-of-thought reasoning natively—extra step-by-step instructions often add redundant verbosity. Constrain the final output format, length, and epistemic honesty instead.

faq.q: Can I use AgentTune's 43 MIT personality templates with DeepSeek?
faq.a: Yes. Open any profile in the AgentTune library or Custom Instructions Generator and select API / Markdown export to wrap the behavioral rules cleanly inside your DeepSeek system message.
